tests.title: af fix or triage with neither --local nor --workspace exits 2 naming both modes, with the hint depending on whether a server is named
given: a temp working dir
a recording fake forge and a recording fake service
tests.when: `af fix <issue url>` and `af triage 42` are run with no mode, once with AF_URL set and once with it unset
then: status is usage and exit code is 2
error.message names `--workspace`, `--server`, `AF_URL` and `--local`
error.fix_hint is {flag:"--workspace"} when a server is named and {flag:"--local"} otherwise
tests.pseudocode: for cmd in [fix,triage]: for url in [set,unset]: env=run(cmd,input); assert env.status=='usage' and exit==2; assert hint.flag == ('--workspace' if url else '--local')

tests.title: --local together with --workspace is a usage error naming both flags
given: a recording fake service
tests.when: `af fix 42 --local --workspace widgets` and `af triage 42 --workspace=w --local` are run
then: status usage, exit code 2
message names `--local` and `--workspace`
tests.pseudocode: env=run('fix','42','--local','--workspace','widgets'); assert exit==2; assert '--local' in msg and '--workspace' in msg

tests.title: A refused mode invocation reaches neither the forge nor the service and creates no run directory
given: a recording fake forge, a recording fake service, GITHUB_TOKEN set and AF_URL naming the fake
an empty working dir
tests.when: invocations refused by R1 or R2 are run: no mode, both modes, `--local --wait`, `--workspace` with `--dir`, and no server
then: every one exits 2
the forge recorded zero requests
the service recorded zero requests
no `.agent-fox/run/` directory exists under the working dir or --dir
tests.pseudocode: for args in refused: run(args); assert forge.requests==[] and svc.requests==[]; assert not exists('.agent-fox/run')

tests.title: Words after `--` are the input and never a mode, and only words before it are scanned
given: a recording fake service
tests.when: `af triage -- --local` and `af fix --workspace widgets -- 42`  and `af triage x -- --workspace` are run
then: `-- --local` names no mode: exit 2 with the no-mode message
`--workspace widgets -- 42` chooses service mode
a `--workspace` after `--` is not read as a mode: exit 2 no-mode message
tests.pseudocode: assert run('triage','--','--local').exit==2; assert mode('fix','--workspace','widgets','--','42')=='service'

tests.title: A mode word that is the value of a value-taking flag is that flag's value
given: a recording fake service and forge
tests.when: `af triage x --context --local`, `af triage x --context --workspace w`, `af fix 1 --output --local` and `af fix 1 --emit-events=--local` are run
then: the first three name no mode and exit 2
no forge or service request is sent and no run directory is created
`--local` is accepted as the value of the flag in each case rather than as a mode
tests.pseudocode: env=run('triage','x','--context','--local'); assert env.exit==2 and 'no mode' semantics

tests.title: Mode flags are read with one or two dashes, and a missing or empty --workspace value is a usage error
given: a fake service that accepts queue requests
tests.when: `--workspace w`, `-workspace w`, `--workspace=w` and `-workspace=w` are given, then `--workspace` as the last word, `--workspace=` and `--workspace ''`
then: the first four choose service mode
the last three exit 2 with a message naming `--workspace`
tests.pseudocode: for form in forms: assert mode(form)=='service'; for bad in [last,'--workspace=',empty]: assert exit==2 and '--workspace' in msg

tests.title: --local follows Go boolean syntax: true values choose local, false counts as not given, garbage is a usage error
given: a fake forge
tests.when: `--local`, `--local=true`, `-local=1`, `--local=false` (alone and with --workspace w) and `--local=maybe` are given
then: `--local`, `--local=true`, `-local=1` choose local mode
`--local=false` alone is the no-mode usage error; with --workspace it chooses service mode
`--local=maybe` exits 2 with a message naming `--local`
tests.pseudocode: assert mode('--local=true')=='local'; assert run('--local=false').exit==2; assert '--local' in run('--local=maybe').msg

tests.title: Help for triage and fix describes both modes and each mode's flags
given: no forge or service
tests.when: `af triage --help`, `af help triage`, `af fix --help` and `af help fix` are run
then: each exits 0
the text mentions `--local`, `--workspace`, `--server`, `--wait` and the loop-only flags
`af triage x --context --help` still treats --help as the context value
tests.pseudocode: for a in forms: out=run(a); assert exit==0; assert all(t in out for t in ['--local','--workspace','--server','--wait'])

tests.title: Local mode refuses --server and --wait with a usage error naming the flag
given: a recording fake forge and service
tests.when: `af fix 42 --local --server http://x`, `af triage 42 --local --wait` are run
then: status usage, exit code 2
message names the refused flag
no forge read, no service request, no run directory
tests.pseudocode: for flag in ['--server http://x','--wait']: env=run(...); assert exit==2 and flag_name in msg; assert no_traces()

tests.title: Service mode refuses every loop-only flag, naming it, and sends no request
given: a recording fake service
tests.when: for each of --dir, --repo, --dry-run, --land, --brain, --sandbox, --borrowed-hands, --budget, --max-turns, --script (both commands), --label (triage) and --base, --attempts, --no-verify (fix), the command is run with --workspace w
then: each exits 2 with status usage
the message names that flag
no request is sent
tests.pseudocode: for (cmd,flag) in table: env=run(cmd,'1','--workspace','w',flag,val); assert exit==2 and flag in msg; assert svc.requests==[]

tests.title: --context, --timeout, --output and --emit-events are accepted on triage and fix in both modes
given: a fake service that queues jobs
a stubbed local loop
tests.when: each of the four flags is added to a `--workspace` and to a `--local` invocation of both commands
then: none of them yields a usage error about that flag in either mode
tests.pseudocode: for mode in modes: for flag in four: assert not usage_error_naming(flag)

tests.title: Local mode behaves exactly as before the spec even with AF_URL on a closed port
given: scripted brain and fake forge as used by the existing local triage and fix tests
AF_URL set to a closed local port
tests.when: `af fix <issue> --local` and `af triage <issue> --local` run with the same flags as the pre-spec baseline
then: statuses, exit codes, results, events, warnings and run directory contents equal the pre-spec golden outputs
the only envelope difference is triage's fix suggestion in next
no connection to the closed port is attempted
tests.pseudocode: env=run('fix',url,'--local',...); assert normalize(env)==baseline; assert port_attempts==0

tests.title: Triage's fix suggestion ends with --local, from the loop and from triage land
given: a scripted triage ending in a confirmed diagnosis and another in a probable diagnosis
a prepared run for `af triage land`
tests.when: triage runs with --local and `af triage land` is run
then: next contains argv ["af","fix",<issue url>,"--dir",<dir>,"--local"] exactly
running that argv does not give the no-mode usage error
tests.pseudocode: assert hasNext(env, ['af','fix',url,'--dir',dir,'--local'])

tests.title: An in-process invocation of the loops without --local still runs and never contacts a service
given: a fresh toolio.App with the loops registered as the worker does
a recording fake service named by AF_URL
tests.when: the loops are invoked in process with flags and no --local or --workspace
then: the loop runs as before (no no-mode usage error)
the service recorded zero requests
the existing worker invocation tests pass unchanged
tests.pseudocode: app=newInProcessApp(); env=app.Main(['af','fix',url,'--dir',d]); assert env.status != usage_nomode; assert svc.requests==[]

tests.title: Every new command registers a schema and the golden matches --schema output byte for byte
given: the registered af app
cmd/af/testdata/schema.golden.json
tests.when: `--schema` is produced for every command and compared with the golden; the schemas for the job result, job page, subscription view, {workspaces}, {slug} and {credential_file, server} are validated against sample results with extra fields
then: output equals the golden byte for byte
samples with unknown extra fields validate
`af triage --schema` and `af fix --schema` validate both a local result and a job result
each schema's top-level properties match its Go result type's JSON fields
tests.pseudocode: assert dumpSchemas()==read(golden); for s in samples: assert validate(s.schema, s.doc)

tests.title: A docs test finds every required term in the documentation and no checked phrase is removed
given: docs/cli.md, docs/configuration.md, docs/model-usage.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/development.md, README.md, docs/errata/16_*.md
tests.when: the docs test reads each file
then: cli.md holds the mode rule, new commands and flags, the categories service, conflict, hub, job_cancelled, the warnings server_insecure, credential_file_permissions, attempt_envelope_unavailable, the event job_event, `af fix <issue url> --dir <dir> --local` and the registered command count
configuration.md and model-usage.md name AF_URL, ~/.af/config.toml, token and result.job.usage
architecture, development and README name the client
existing docs tests still pass
tests.pseudocode: for (file,terms) in required: for t in terms: assert t in read(file)

tests.title: --server wins over AF_URL and an empty AF_URL counts as unset
given: two scripted fake services A and B
tests.when: a service command runs with --server A and AF_URL=B; then with only AF_URL=B; then with AF_URL='' and no flag
then: the first sends its requests only to A
the second sends to B
the third is the no-server usage error
tests.pseudocode: assert hits(A)>0 and hits(B)==0; ...; assert run().exit==2

tests.title: An http or https server with a path prefix is accepted and one trailing slash is dropped
given: a scripted fake service under a path prefix /prefix
tests.when: the server is given as `http://127.0.0.1:P/prefix/` and `http://127.0.0.1:P/prefix`
then: requests go to `/prefix/api/v1/...` with no double slash
`https://` URLs with a host are accepted
tests.pseudocode: assert recorded.path.startswith('/prefix/api/v1/')

tests.title: A malformed server URL is a usage error naming its source and the rule, and sends nothing
given: a recording fake service
tests.when: the server is `localhost:80`, `ftp://h`, `http://`, `http://h/?q=1`, `http://h/#f`, `http://u:p@h`, once via --server and once via AF_URL
then: status usage, exit code 2
message names `--server` or `AF_URL` according to the source, and the broken rule
the password of a user-info URL never appears in the output
no request is sent
tests.pseudocode: for u in bad: for src in [flag,env]: env=run(src,u); assert exit==2 and src_name in msg

tests.title: A service command with no server is a usage error naming --server and AF_URL, plus --local for triage and fix
given: AF_URL unset
a valid credential file
tests.when: `af workspace list` and `af fix 1 --workspace w` are run
then: status usage, exit code 2, fix_hint {flag:"--server", env:"AF_URL"}
the message of the fix command also names `--local`
nothing is sent
tests.pseudocode: env=run('workspace','list'); assert env.error.fix_hint=={'flag':'--server','env':'AF_URL'}

tests.title: A non-loopback http server raises server_insecure and the command continues; loopback does not
given: a fake transport answering 200 for any host
tests.when: `af workspace list` is run with servers http://example.com, http://localhost:1, http://127.0.0.2:1, http://[::1]:1 and https://example.com
then: only http://example.com raises warning server_insecure
the command still completes with exit 0
tests.pseudocode: assert ('server_insecure' in codes(run(u))) == (u=='http://example.com')

tests.title: The request carries the top-level token of ~/.af/config.toml and other keys are ignored
given: HOME holds .af/config.toml with other keys, a table with its own `token`, and a top-level token `T1`
a scripted fake service
tests.when: `af workspace list` is run
then: Authorization is `Bearer T1`
other keys and the table's token are ignored
tests.pseudocode: assert svc.last.header['Authorization']=='Bearer T1'

tests.title: An unfindable home or unreadable credential file fails io naming the path before any request
given: a recording fake service
(a) no HOME, (b) the credential path is a directory, (c) the file has mode 000 (non-root, Unix)
tests.when: `af workspace list` is run in each case
then: status failed, exit code 1, category io
message names the path
no request is sent
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: env=run(); assert env.exit==1 and env.error.category=='io'; assert svc.requests==[]

tests.title: A missing file or a missing, non-string or empty token fails auth with the login hint
given: a recording fake service
cases: no file, no token key, token = 5, token = ""
tests.when: `af workspace list` is run in each case
then: status failed, exit code 1, category auth
message names the file and says to run `af login --token-file FILE` or `afc login`
fix_hint is {suggest:"af login --token-file FILE"}
no request is sent
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: env=run(); assert env.error.category=='auth' and env.error.fix_hint.suggest=='af login --token-file FILE'

tests.title: A credential file that is not TOML, or a token with a line break or control character, fails config
given: a recording fake service
cases: `token = ` garbage, a token containing \n, a token containing \x07
tests.when: `af workspace list` is run in each case
then: status failed, exit code 1, category config
message names the file
no request is sent and the token value is not echoed
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: env=run(); assert env.error.category=='config'

tests.title: On Unix a group- or other-accessible credential file raises credential_file_permissions and the command goes on
given: a credential file with mode 0644, a second with 0600
a fake service answering 200
tests.when: `af workspace list` is run with each
then: 0644 raises warning credential_file_permissions naming the file, exit 0
0600 raises no such warning
tests.pseudocode: assert 'credential_file_permissions' in codes(run(mode=0o644)); assert not in codes(run(mode=0o600))

tests.title: A credential and a workspace PAT never appear in any output
given: a scripted fake service that sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails, and may echo request headers or bodies into error messages
tests.when: for any command among login, workspace subscribe, jobs and fix --workspace --wait, any sentinel credential and PAT, and any answer of the service
then: the sentinel credential and sentinel PAT are absent from stdout, stderr, the --output file, the --emit-events file, every error message and every warning
tests.pseudocode: for cmd,cred,pat,answer in gen(): out=run(cmd,--output o,--emit-events e); for s in [cred,pat]: for f in [stdout,stderr,o,e]: assert s not in f

tests.title: The credential reaches only the server's host, even when the service redirects elsewhere
given: a scripted service A that redirects to a second recording server B
tests.when: `af workspace list --server A` runs
then: B received no request
no request to any host other than A carries the Authorization header
tests.pseudocode: assert B.requests==[]

tests.title: af login reads the credential from a file or stdin, never the command line, and an unreadable source is io
given: a fake service answering 200 to the check
a token file, a missing path, a stdin that errors
tests.when: `af login --token-file f`, `--token-file -`, `--token-file missing`, and stdin read failure are run
then: the first two succeed with the file's/stdin's token on the check request
the missing path and the stdin failure are status failed, exit 1, category io naming the path or stdin
no argument other than --token-file's value is taken as a credential: a positional argument is refused
tests.pseudocode: assert svc.check.header=='Bearer '+tok; assert run('login','--token-file','missing').error.category=='io'

tests.title: An empty, multi-line, control-character or oversized credential is a usage error and nothing is written
given: a fake service
a HOME with no credential file
tests.when: af login reads a token file that is blank, has two lines, holds \x01, or is 4097 bytes; and one of exactly 4096 bytes
then: the bad ones: status usage, exit code 2, message names `--token-file`, no request and no file written
the 4096-byte token passes the content rule
surrounding whitespace and one trailing newline are trimmed
tests.pseudocode: for t in bad: assert run(t).exit==2 and '--token-file' in msg; assert not exists(config)

tests.title: An unreadable, unparsable or wrongly laid-out existing credential file fails without a check request and stays byte-identical
given: existing files: unreadable (mode 000), invalid TOML, no token line, token only after a [table], token with a multi-line string, `token = "a" "b"`, token via dotted key
a recording fake service
tests.when: `af login --token-file f` is run against each
then: io for unreadable, config for the others, status failed, exit 1
layout message names the file, says its layout is not the one af expects and that `afc login` or an edit fixes it
no request to the service
the file's bytes are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: before=read(cfg); env=run(); assert env.error.category==case.cat; assert read(cfg)==before; assert svc.requests==[]

tests.title: After the local checks pass, af login sends GET /api/v1/workspaces with the new credential and accepts any 2xx
given: a scripted service answering 200, 204-like 2xx variants
tests.when: `af login --token-file f` is run
then: exactly one request: GET /api/v1/workspaces with `Authorization: Bearer <new token>`
a 2xx answer proceeds to the write
tests.pseudocode: assert svc.requests==[('GET','/api/v1/workspaces')]

tests.title: A 401 on the check fails auth saying the credential was refused and writes nothing
given: a service answering 401
(a) no credential file, (b) an existing file
tests.when: `af login --token-file f` is run
then: status failed, exit code 1, category auth
message says the service refused this credential
no file is created and an existing one is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.category=='auth' and 'refused' in msg; assert unchanged(cfg)

tests.title: A 502, other answer, transport error or timeout on the check says the credential was not checked and writes nothing
given: services answering 502, 500, 404, a closed port, and one that stalls past the request bound (injected clock)
tests.when: `af login --token-file f` is run against each
then: a 502 gives status failed, exit 1, category hub, retryable true
others follow the 16-REQ-6.5 table
the message says the credential could not be checked and never says refused
the credential file is unchanged or absent
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.category=='hub' and env.error.retryable; assert 'could not be checked' in msg and 'refused' not in msg

tests.title: A first login writes mode 0600 and a re-login replaces only the token value, keeping every other byte
given: a fake service answering 200
HOME without ~/.af; then a file with comments, other keys, a table and a literal-string `token = 'old'  # note` line
a credential containing quotes and backslashes
tests.when: `af login --token-file -` is run twice
then: first: ~/.af created 0700, config.toml is exactly `token = "<cred>"` with mode 0600
second: only the value on the token line changes, to a TOML basic string; all other bytes (comments, keys, tables, CRLF endings) are identical; mode 0600
result is {credential_file, server} and never contains the credential; exit 0
the file parses back to the same token
tests.pseudocode: assert read(cfg)==expected; assert stat(cfg).mode==0o600; assert toml.decode(read(cfg))['token']==cred; assert cred not in stdout

tests.title: Each write-phase failure is io naming the path, removes the temp file and leaves the existing file intact
given: injected failures in turn: creating ~/.af, writing the temp file, sync, close, rename
a service answering 200
an existing credential file
tests.when: `af login --token-file f` is run for each failure
then: status failed, exit code 1, category io
message names the path
no temp file remains in ~/.af
the existing file's bytes are unchanged
tests.pseudocode: for fault in faults: env=run(fault); assert env.error.category=='io'; assert listdir(.af)==['config.toml']; assert read(cfg)==before

tests.title: An invocation with several local mistakes reports the first in the fixed order, and sends nothing
given: a recording fake service
a missing credential file and no server
tests.when: commands carrying combined mistakes are run: (flag error + bad input + bad server + no credential), (bad input + bad server + no credential), (bad server + no credential), (no server + no credential), and for login (bad token file content + existing bad file)
then: each reports the earliest failing check: flags, then input/arguments, then server, then credential (or for login the existing file)
a usage mistake is always reported before an auth or config failure
no request is sent in any case
tests.pseudocode: assert run(flag_err,bad_input,bad_url).msg mentions flag; assert run(bad_input,bad_url).msg mentions input; ...

tests.title: Every request carries the bearer, User-Agent and Accept headers, and bodies are JSON
given: a recording fake service
App.Identity version V
tests.when: a PUT subscribe, a POST queue, a GET job and a GET events stream are issued
then: all carry Authorization Bearer <credential> and User-Agent `af/V`
events request has Accept text/event-stream, the others application/json
requests with a body carry Content-Type application/json
tests.pseudocode: for r in svc.requests: assert r.UA=='af/'+V; assert r.accept == ('text/event-stream' if events else 'application/json')

tests.title: Requests are bounded by 2 minutes or the remaining --timeout, bodies by 8 MiB, and --timeout has no default
given: an injected clock
a service that never answers
a service that returns a body over 8 MiB
tests.when: a plain request runs without --timeout, then with --timeout 5s, then the oversized body is fetched
then: without --timeout the request is cut at 2 minutes with category service, retryable true
with --timeout 5s the command ends at 5 s with the shell's timeout failure
the oversized body gives category service, retryable false, and no more than 8 MiB is read
no default --timeout applies to any client command
tests.pseudocode: clock.advance(120s); assert env.error=={'service',retryable:true}; assert bytesRead<=8*MiB

tests.title: A 3xx is not followed and is mapped as a non-retryable service failure
given: a scripted service answering 301, 302, 307 and 308 with a Location pointing at a recording server
tests.when: `af workspace get w` is run
then: status failed, exit code 1, category service, retryable false
the Location target recorded no request
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.category=='service' and not env.error.retryable; assert target.requests==[]

tests.title: Each row of the answer table gives its status, exit code, category and retryable flag
given: a scripted service that answers the chosen status for `af workspace get w`
tests.when: the service answers 400, 401, 404, 409, 422, 502, 500, 503, 504, 507, 405, 413, 415, 418, a dropped connection, and a 200 whose body is not JSON
then: 400 and 404: usage, exit 2, category usage, not retryable
401 and 422: failed, exit 1, category auth, not retryable
409: failed, category conflict, not retryable
502: failed, category hub, retryable
500: failed, category service, not retryable
503, 504, 507: failed, category service, retryable
405, 413, 415, 418: failed, category service, not retryable
transport error: failed, service, retryable
non-JSON 200: failed, service, not retryable
tests.pseudocode: for (status,exp) in table: env=run(answer=status); assert (env.status,env.exit,env.error.category,env.error.retryable)==exp

tests.title: Failure messages carry the service message and code, the server source for transport errors, and the thing a 404 asked for
given: a scripted service
tests.when: it answers {error:{code:"invalid_request",message:"bad"}}, then an empty 500 body, then 404 for job j and for workspace w; and a transport error with --server and with AF_URL
then: message is `bad (invalid_request)`
an empty body gives `the service answered 500`
a 404 names the job id or the slug and says it does not exist or hub does not let the caller see it
a transport error names the server URL and `--server` or `AF_URL` accordingly
tests.pseudocode: assert msg=='bad (invalid_request)'; assert 'j' in msg404job; assert '--server' in transportMsgFlag

tests.title: Failures carry the fix hint of their answer
given: a scripted service
tests.when: it answers 401, 404 on a workspace route, 409 not_subscribed, 409 token_unreadable, 409 invalid_state, 404 on a job route, and 422
then: 401: {suggest:"af login --token-file FILE"}
404 on workspace route, 409 not_subscribed and token_unreadable: {suggest:"af workspace subscribe <slug> --hub-token-file FILE"} with the real slug
422: {flag:"--hub-token-file"}
409 invalid_state and a 404 on a job route carry no such hint
tests.pseudocode: assert env.error.fix_hint==expected

tests.title: Service documents reach results as received, unknown fields included
given: a scripted service returning job, page and subscription documents with extra unknown fields and nested values

then: result.job, the page and the subscription view hold every field of the document, including unknown ones, with equal values

tests.title: Each input form of af triage --workspace becomes the right request field
given: a recording service answering 202
an existing regular file notes.txt
tests.when: inputs `-` (stdin), `https://github.com/o/r/issues/1`, `http://example.org/x`, `42`, `#42`, `o/r#7`, `a/b/c#7`, `notes.txt`, `some words` and `7x` are given

`42` and `#42`: {issue: 42} as a JSON number
`o/r#7` and `a/b/c#7`: {issue:"o/r#7"} as a string
`notes.txt`: {file:{name:"notes.txt", content}}
`some words` and `7x`: {text}

tests.title: af fix --workspace accepts only issue forms and refuses text, files and stdin with a usage error
given: a recording service
an existing file and free text
tests.when: `af fix --workspace w` gets `-`, `notes.txt`, `some words`, then N, #N, owner/repo#N and an issue URL
then: the first three: usage, exit 2, message says af fix takes `N`, `#N`, `owner/repo#N` or an issue URL, no request
the last four are sent as issue

tests.title: Empty, NUL, invalid UTF-8 and directory inputs are usage errors and an unreadable file is io, all before any request
given: a recording service
stdin and files with whitespace only, a NUL byte, bytes 0xff 0xfe, a directory, and a file with mode 000
tests.when: `af triage --workspace w <input>` is run with each
then: empty, NUL, invalid UTF-8, directory: status usage, exit 2
unreadable file: status failed, exit 1, category io
no request is sent
tests.pseudocode: for case in cases: env=run(case); assert (env.exit,cat)==case.expected; assert svc.requests==[]

tests.title: Over-long content is cut at a UTF-8 boundary so content plus marker fits MaxInputBytes
given: a recording service
content of 131072+1000 bytes of 3-byte runes, and content of exactly 131072 bytes
tests.when: it is sent as stdin text and as a file
then: the sent content length is at most 131072 bytes and is valid UTF-8
the content ends with the truncation marker
envelope input.truncated is true and warning input_truncated is raised
content of exactly 131072 bytes is sent unchanged with truncated false
tests.pseudocode: assert len(sent)<=131072 and utf8.valid(sent); assert env.input.truncated and 'input_truncated' in codes

tests.title: The envelope's input reports kind, origin and truncated for each input form

origin is the URL for the URL, the absolute path for the file, and "" otherwise
truncated is reported for each

tests.title: The body is posted to the workspace's triage or fix route with the slug escaped and --context values in order
given: a recording service answering 202

tests.title: A 202 records the job artifact at once and without --wait finishes done with next pointing at watch
given: a scripted service answering 202 with a job document

next is `af jobs watch <id>` with `--server <url>` only when the server came from the flag

tests.title: A 409 duplicate_job fails conflict with the service's message naming the open job

tests.title: workspace subscribe sends the PAT and optional prefix, and treats 201 and 200 as success

tests.title: Bad PAT files fail before any request: io for read failures, usage for content rules

tests.title: workspace list, get and unsubscribe use their routes and return their results

tests.pseudocode: assert env.result=={'slug':'w'}; assert run('workspace','get','BAD!').exit==2

tests.title: jobs list picks the route, passes state and cursor only when given, and next repeats the command with the next cursor

tests.title: jobs get, cancel, retry and answer send their requests and return {job, envelope:null}; --wait follows with the job recorded
given: a scripted service that answers each job route and serves a short event stream for --wait

tests.title: jobs answer with no answer or with more than one is a usage error and sends nothing

tests.title: A 409 on a job command fails conflict with the service message and the fix hint

tests.title: The SSE reader frames id, event and data lines, ignores comments and unknown fields, and accepts 1 MiB lines

tests.title: Events with seq not above the last delivered are dropped and each delivered event is emitted as job_event

tests.title: A stream end of any kind is followed by a job read, and following ends only when that read says at rest
given: scripted streams ending by EOF, a dropped connection, an unreadable frame, and 60 s of silence on an injected clock

at rest ends the following

tests.title: Failed tries count by cause and the delay before each try is 1, 2, 4, 8 s, or 1 s after a try that delivered an event
given: an injected clock that records sleeps

a delivering try resets the count so the next failure waits 1 s
every cause listed counts as a failed try

tests.title: A 401, 404, 3xx or other 4xx during following stops at once with the R6 mapping

tests.title: For any pattern of cuts and duplicate frames every event is delivered exactly once in ascending order
